rules.sentence: Traumatic muscular hematomas will typically resolve spontaneously.
However, if a patient does develop a hematoma as a result of a trauma, the patient may benefit from evaluation from a trained medical provider to assess for other injuries.
Patients who develop a spontaneous muscular hematoma should be evaluated by a healthcare professional who can carefully weigh the risks and benefits of all treatment options.
Anticoagulation therapy should only be stopped by a clinician who knows all medical comorbidities in play, as decisions in management are determined on a case-by-case basis.
Traumatic muscular hematomas are often the result of a traumatic injury, and therefore should be met with thorough evaluation for traumatic injuries by an appropriate provider.
Spontaneous muscular hematomas similarly require an interdisciplinary approach to achieve the best outcomes.

For example, stopping anticoagulation therapy may be suitable for the management of a patient's spontaneous muscular hematoma but is not reasonable from the perspective of his or her other medical comorbidities.
